LESSON: SCANNING BY PARAGRAPH AND PAGE NUMBERS TO LOCATE INFORMATION.

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Braille Reading Skills
Topic 2.1: Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information.
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information., part of Braille Reading Skills in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: Why is scanning through a Braille document important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify contracted and uncontracted Braille signs in writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. differentiate between contracted and uncontracted Braille in writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use contracted and uncontracted Braille signs in writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate using contracted and uncontracted Braille signs in writing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information. in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify contracted and uncontracted Braille signs in writing,

   Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information. helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. differentiate between contracted and uncontracted Braille in writing,

   Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information. helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. use contracted and uncontracted Braille signs in writing,

   Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information. helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate using contracted and uncontracted Braille signs in writing.

   Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information. helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on a provided passage to explain ways of scanning by page or paragraphs (identifying starts of paragraphs, exploring by use of one hand, exploring using both hands, tracking with fingers from left to right or up to bottom,),

2. interact with Braille books or articles and read Braille texts and share with peers for feedback,

3. read and exchange different Braille passages or books with peers to evaluate their scanning skills and share for feedback.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on a provided passage to explain ways of scanning by page or paragraphs (identifying starts of paragraphs, exploring by use of one hand, exploring using both hands, tracking with fingers from left to right or up to bottom,),
2. interact with Braille books or articles and read Braille texts and share with peers for feedback,
3. read and exchange different Braille passages or books with peers to evaluate their scanning skills and share for feedback.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Scanning by Paragraph and Page Numbers to Locate Information. together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: as learners interact with Braille books or articles and read Braille texts and share with peers for

feedback,

● Self-efficacy: as learners read and exchange different Braille passages or books with peers to evaluate their scanning

skills and share for feedback,

7

Values:
● Responsibility: as learners interact with Braille books or articles and read Braille texts and share with peers for feedback.

● Love: as learners interact with Braille books or articles and read Braille texts and with love share with peers for feedback.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Peer education: Learners read and exchange different Braille passages or books with peers to evaluate their scanning

skills and share feedback.

● social cohesion: learners work in groups or pairs to read and exchange different Braille passages or books with peers

to evaluate their scanning skills and share feedback.
